# <span id="aanchor410"></span> Audits

Audits allow users to define criteria for meters to be flagged for audit on a meter by meter basis. The criteria can be based on:

- Time (monthly, quarterly, semi-annually, or annually)
- Volume or energy change from one month to the next
- Total volume or energy for the month
- Difference in volume or energy for a check to sales relationship (meter or check location)

Before starting, consider the following questions:

- Is this for volume recovery or a second layer of data validation?
- Will individual analysts or a small group manage the setup and review?
- Is there a current list of ins and outs for gathering systems or one-to-one relationships for checks on sales meters?
- Will this roll out to one geographic area or one-to-one relationships first?

This feature requires the **Audit Package** module.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 610;height: 538;" />

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Configure">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Configuring a Meter to Audit</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Configure">

A meter’s audit criteria can be set up within the Meter Editor \> Audits tab, to validate potential discrepancies with an Audit, Custody, or Check Meter.

Audits can be performed based on volume/energy differences or using a time criteria.

<div class="procedure">

To configure a meter to audit based on volume/energy values:

1.  Go to **Setup** \> **Meter Editor**.
2.  Select a meter to audit and click **Edit**.
3.  Select the **Audits** tab.
4.  Select the Audit Meter the user will be doing the audit work in. The Audit Meter is for informational purposes only and will not generate audits.
5.  Select a Check Meter or location to compare with.
6.  Select the Auditor from the user list that will be primarily perform audits of the meter.
7.  Select the Contact who will be contacted for information on the meter.
8.  Select Volume or Energy limit.
9.  Enter a value for the Monthly change greater than field.
10. Enter a value for the Check meter differs by field.

You can audit on any one of the available parameters or a combination.

If Frequency is selected, audits will be created at the frequency regardless of any other criteria. The user will need to select a month/year to begin the frequency validation.  
  
Only monthly volumes are considered, not daily. Audits will not automatically kick-out if the data is incomplete for the month.

 

</div>

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Viewing Editing">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Viewing or Editing an Audit</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Viewing Editing">

Audits that have been flagged by the Audit service can be viewed from the Audit Tracker screen. Users can also create an audit manually from the Audit Tracker.

From the Audit Tracker the user can walk through the audit process, starting from identifying the problem, to requesting data from a third party, or requesting an adjustment, to closing out the audit.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 589;height: 418;" />

<div class="procedure">

To access the Audit Tracker and view audits:

1.  Go to **Tools** \> **Audits**.
2.  Filter by meter, list, or location, contact, auditor, customer, result, or status.
3.  Click **Refresh**. Audits are created with a default status of ‘Need to Request Data’.
4.  Double-click the record to make edits in the Audit Detail screen. For example, edit the Auditor, Audit Status, Note, or Problem Found. Notes can be used to detail findings and document action items and results. The Problem Found can be populated when an audit is resolved.

</div>

#### Audit Tracker Data Field Details

- **Detail View** - Double clicking a record within Audit Tracker or selecting the Detail View button will open the Audit Detail screen.
- **New Audit** - Manually create an audit
- **Refresh** - Refresh screen
- **Print** - Preview the full audit package for the audit selected, which includes the Audit Reconciliation Request, GVS Daily, Audit Data Request Letter, and Audit Summary reports.
- **Exit** - Exit screen

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Details">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Audit Detail</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Details">

Double clicking a record within Audit Tracker or selecting the **Detail View** button will open the Audit Detail screen. This screen shows:

- The meter flagged for audit
- The month being audited
- Why it was flagged
- Who the assigned auditor is
- Who the primary contact is
- The status of the audit
- Volume and energy for the meter being audited, the check meter/location and the audit meter

#### Data Field Details

- **Audit Criteria** - Click the button to see the full audit criteria as specified in the Meter Editor
- **Status History** - Click the button to view the dates for different steps in the progression of the audit
- **Problem Found - Select** - Click Select to select, edit, or create a Problem Code and Description. Once a problem is found, choose a Problem Found for the audit.
- **Letter** - Print or send a letter requesting data to the contact. See: Letter Selection
- **Save** - Save changes
- **Custom** - View or edit the 15 custom fields associated to the audit. The labels for these fields can be customized within the User-Defined Labels screen under the Settings Manager. There is an Audits tab that will allow changing the labels. Users must have System Information privilege to access the editor.
- **Exit** - Exit form
- **Print** - At any step in the process, the user can click Print to preview the Audit Detail report. The report will show information from the audit and as the audit progresses and more information is available, will reflect changes to the audit.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Letter Selection">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Letter Selection</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Letter Selection">

Once the audit work has determined the problem, the user can send a letter from FLOWCAL requesting an adjustment. Clicking the Letter button on the Audit Detail screen will open the Letter Selection screen.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 278;height: 315;" />

##### Data Field Details

- **Letters for Need to Request Data** - Letter to request data or an adjustment

After requesting data, the user can change the Audit Status to Data Requested. Once data is received, work can be done in the audit meter to determine the reason for the difference.

Once the Audit Status has changed from Data Requested, the Request Adjustment option is available for selection.

- **Contact Methods** - The contact selected on the Audits tab within Meter Editor will be displayed.
  - **Print** - Generate a local print of the letter
  - **Email** - If the contact has an email address defined, it will be displayed.
- **Preview** - Preview the letter requesting data

</div>
